traps.shape: personality path with '..' segments, and a path that shares the mount point's leading characters but names a sibling directory
traps.realistic_because: the reported site; absolute and relative personality paths are a normal API use (lstrip('/') rebases absolute paths), so a containment rule must keep both

traps.shape: in-image directory or file that is a link to a host path; lexical normalisation alone leaves it open
traps.realistic_because: the how-type mechanism: the image is caller-supplied, so links inside it need resolving, not just '..' normalisation; refusing links outright breaks images that legitimately contain in-root links

traps.shape: refusal that happens only at the write step, after the parent directory was already created
traps.realistic_because: the parent directory is created as root before the write, so a check placed only at the write leaves a host-side directory behind even though the request fails

traps.shape: the fixed root/.ssh directory components are links in the caller-supplied image
traps.realistic_because: a hard-coded destination path looks out of scope, but mkdir/chown/chmod run as root through whatever the image supplies at those components

traps.shape: the fixed etc/network directory components are links in the caller-supplied image
traps.realistic_because: a fixed path with operator-templated content reads as out of scope, yet its mkdir/chown/chmod/tee run as root through the image

traps.shape: the fixed meta.js name is a link in the caller-supplied image
traps.realistic_because: metadata comes from the instance the user creates and the destination name is fixed, so the link in the image is the only user-controlled part

traps.shape: etc/passwd or etc/shadow, or the etc directory itself, is a link in the caller-supplied image; the copy runs in both directions
traps.realistic_because: the route sits behind an optional feature flag and modifies existing files rather than creating arbitrary ones, which makes it look harmless

traps.shape: the legacy protocol-2 key file root/.ssh/authorized_keys2 is a link in the caller-supplied image
traps.realistic_because: injected sibling in the same key-injection path: a maintainer-style compatibility write to the legacy protocol-2 key file, no deceptive naming, reachable only through the real key-injection entry point, covered only by the task's general property, untouched by the published fix
